methods.problem: Use the model's local uncertainty as a transparent first-error signal.
methods.plain_summary: Maps token entropy to step risk without learning a semantic verifier.
methods.input_operation_output: token entropy -> optional causal transform -> step reducer -> one risk per step
methods.novelty: Not a new primitive; it is the transparent anchor that isolates gains from later machinery.
assumptions: A reasoning error creates a local increase or instability in predictive uncertainty.
limitations: Absolute entropy can be high on difficult but correct steps and low on confidently wrong steps.

methods.problem: Balance heterogeneous token signals without allowing large feature families to dominate.
methods.plain_summary: Averages broad token views inside six provenance families before localization.
methods.input_operation_output: 28 token views -> six provenance-family means -> level curve -> step risk
methods.novelty: Provenance balancing, coupled to a dedicated local step reducer.
assumptions: Signal provenance is more stable than individual reconstructed coordinates.
limitations: The historical 0.3662 system also used a separate complete-answer detector.

methods.problem: Fuse the modern 29-stream token representation without target labels.
methods.plain_summary: Fits the registered ordinary IU covariance fusion and reduces token risk within each step.
methods.input_operation_output: 29 standardized token streams -> ordinary IU weights -> token risk -> step maximum
methods.novelty: Modern common-protocol incumbent used as a reference, not a new claim in this program.
assumptions: A shared low-rank correctness direction is identifiable from target-free dependence.
limitations: The 29-stream contract contains both exact and best-effort reconstructed coordinates.

methods.problem: Detect sudden local deterioration rather than high absolute uncertainty.
methods.plain_summary: EMA-smooths a token evidence proxy and aggregates its strongest negative first differences.
methods.input_operation_output: top-k entropy evidence -> EMA span 5 -> local drops -> step risk
methods.novelty: A direct same-contract adaptation of temporal evidence drop to ProcessBench first-error F1.
assumptions: The first reasoning failure appears as an abrupt evidence loss.
limitations: The paper leaves token-to-step aggregation and clean handling underspecified.

methods.problem: Capture local uncertainty bursts that absolute entropy averages can hide.
methods.plain_summary: Computes causal variance over either a fixed trailing window or one length-adaptive window.
methods.input_operation_output: entropy history up to token t -> trailing variance -> token/step risk
methods.novelty: Reintroduces an early robust signal as a minimal causal localizer rather than a response scalar.
assumptions: Error onset increases short-range entropy volatility.
limitations: Fixed and adaptive windows are separate sensitivity arms and may not be combined post hoc.

methods.problem: Locate a sustained change in entropy without using the completed trace mean.
methods.plain_summary: Accumulates deviations from a label-blind donor center using prefix-only information.
methods.input_operation_output: entropy prefix + donor center -> absolute cumulative deviation -> step risk
methods.novelty: Repairs the historical full-trace-mean CUSUM for a valid causal lane.
assumptions: Error onset induces a persistent mean shift relative to calibration donors.
limitations: CUSUM was weak in prior early-prefix ablations and therefore remains targeted rather than core.

methods.problem: Measure whether the actually sampled token is unexpectedly unlikely.
methods.plain_summary: Uses negative sampled-token log probability as a compact complement to distribution entropy.
methods.input_operation_output: sampled-token log probability -> oriented surprisal curve -> step risk
methods.novelty: Tests sampled-token energy atomically before allowing it into a DSP block.
assumptions: Some errors manifest in the chosen token even when aggregate entropy is modest.
limitations: Existing evidence supports the family more than this source as an independent winner.

methods.problem: Add a distribution-scale energy view complementary to entropy and sampled-token surprisal.
methods.plain_summary: Tracks the registered partition-energy token curve as one atomic source.
methods.input_operation_output: token logit distribution -> partition-energy curve -> step risk
methods.novelty: Tests partition energy separately before any fusion can obscure its contribution.
assumptions: A correctness-relevant energy shift is not fully represented by entropy.
limitations: Historical removal was not harmful on average, so evidence is weak.

methods.problem: Represent level, smoothing, accumulated positive evidence, and persistence without a feature soup.
methods.plain_summary: Crosses three uncertainty sources with four causal transforms for at most 12 coordinates.
methods.input_operation_output: entropy/surprisal/partition energy x level/ewma16/positive area/persistence -> compact fusion -> step risk
methods.novelty: A constrained localization-specific descendant of the successful seven-by-four Unified28 grammar.
assumptions: The useful information lies in a small transform grammar shared across a few sources.
limitations: Unified28 previously regressed on other tasks; DSP12 is not presumed universal.

methods.problem: Localize entropy bursts and rebound events rather than score the whole response.
methods.plain_summary: Converts EDIS burst/rebound morphology into one exploratory onset curve.
methods.input_operation_output: entropy history -> burst/rebound event strength -> onset step risk
methods.novelty: Adapts EDIS from a redundant response scalar into a local temporal diagnostic.
assumptions: Reasoning failures produce identifiable burst or rebound onsets.
limitations: The original window is underspecified and local replications were fragile.

methods.problem: Remove predictable self-history and test whether residual direction localizes errors.
methods.plain_summary: Predicts each token stream from its own lag and fuses the standardized residuals.
methods.input_operation_output: token stream + self lag -> innovation residual -> IU fusion -> step risk
methods.novelty: Retains only the least harmful innovation form after cross-stream rook innovation failed.
assumptions: Unexpected within-stream changes contain complementary error information.
limitations: Prior ProcessBench gain was small and uncertain and PRMBench regressed.

methods.problem: Combine surviving evidence blocks or select coordinates without outcome labels.
methods.plain_summary: Covers equal-family, ordinary IU, SU/STG-SU, DUFS, and transform-hierarchy controls.
methods.input_operation_output: registered evidence blocks -> target-free fusion/selection -> one risk curve
methods.novelty: In the new program fusion is conditional on atomic survival and bounded to three blocks.
assumptions: Surviving sources are complementary and target-free structure identifies useful weights.
limitations: Recent SU/STG/DUFS and hierarchy experiments did not show supported localization gains.

methods.problem: A strong token-risk curve still needs a step score, and the historical top-five mean was selected from a narrow development roster rather than established as optimal.
methods.plain_summary: Holds the token representation, detector, threshold, spans, split, and population fixed; first compares compact within-step aggregators on the identity curve, then permits at most one preregistered causal transform before the selected aggregator.
methods.input_operation_output: frozen token risk r[1:T] -> optional explicit temporal transform T -> registered aggregation A over I_s -> R_s -> argmax_s R_s
methods.novelty: Factorizes temporal transformation from within-step aggregation and tests fixed-k tail means against length-normalized fractions and robust controls without a filter-by-reducer factorial.
assumptions: The frozen reference token curve contains localized evidence whose step readout can be improved without changing detection.
Step-length sensitivity explains part of the difference between fixed-k and length-normalized reducers.
Any useful curve transform survives a matching atomic premise gate before Stage B.
limitations: Planned retrospective development study; no new result or fresh confirmation.
P0-S1 rejects historical step max versus top-five but does not support any other aggregator ordering.
Stage-B templates are non-rankable until Stage A freezes an exact parent and transform parameters.

methods.problem: Fixed within-family means can dilute a useful member view when a surviving provenance family contains several correlated token curves.
methods.plain_summary: Passes singleton entropy through unchanged, compresses each surviving multi-view provenance family with one preregistered calibration-only expert, then combines at most six family scores with one frozen outer U-PCR or IU-PCR rule.
methods.input_operation_output: Phase-2 surviving frozen broad views -> per-family U-PCR/IU-PCR (conditional SU-PCR only after a premise gate; no fusion for singleton entropy) -> one score per surviving family -> one frozen outer U-PCR/IU-PCR -> token risk
methods.novelty: Replaces only the multi-view equal averages in family6 while preserving provenance balance, explicit singleton handling, and a nested no-test-label selection boundary.
assumptions: At least one Phase-2-surviving multi-view family contains complementary member information that an equal mean suppresses.
Calibration-only stability or nested calibration can choose an expert without audit/test F1.
The outer family scores remain sufficiently complementary for a single frozen U-PCR/IU-PCR rule.
limitations: Design proposal only; no completed ProcessBench or PRMBench result.
Prior transform-hierarchy and token SU-PCR variants failed, so this branch is survivor-gated and may not expand beyond the frozen 28-view provenance inventory.
Full-trace CUSUM and STFT-style members are not Phase-5 causal transfers.

methods.problem: Separate complete-answer calibration from relative token-level evidence.
methods.plain_summary: Uses answer-level means and CIW risk to form a bounded token innovation gate.
methods.input_operation_output: token coordinates + answer summaries -> bounded CIW correction -> token fusion
assumptions: Answer-level calibration can improve local evidence after reliability gating.
limitations: It helped PRMBench slightly while hurting ProcessBench, so it is context only here.
